LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Whole Numbers. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LOOK AND LEARN

Activity Count forward by 5 from 5 to 100 Count backward by 5 from 100 to 5

80 75 70 100 95 90 85 5 65 10 60 15 20 55 25 30 35 40 45 50

Work to do 1. Count forward by 5 from 5 to 100.

[[image:/media/pupil-books/grade-2/mathematics/page-149.jpg|Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 2 — page 149]]

From your pupil's book (page 149)

NUMBERS WHOLE NUMBERS Week 1 Lesson 3 Counting

Activity Count forward by 10 from 10 to 100 Count backward by 10 from 100 to 10

Work to do 1. Count forward by 1 0 from 1 1 to 99.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Whole Numbers means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Whole Numbers.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Whole Numbers
2. Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
3. Learning materials: Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 2
4. Revise with the quiz now.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson

   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

2. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. identify place value up to at any point. hundreds.  Learners in pairs / groups to discuss place value up
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

3. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. read numbers 1- in symbols, to hundreds
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

4. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

5. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. Whole Numbers is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

7. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

8. Which statement is true about Whole Numbers?
   A. If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.
   B. We should ignore Whole Numbers at home and school.
   C. Whole Numbers is only for teachers, not learners.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.
